key_insight: Simultaneous neural topology optimization jointly optimizes state, adjoint, and design fields to produce scalable, super-resolution stress-constrained designs.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets material-efficient structural design under stress limits while scaling computation across multiple GPUs.
method: Represent state, adjoint, and design variables with custom neural networks optimized in a single loop.
Combine the design objective, aggregated local stress constraints, and potential energy functionals using continuous adjoints and automatic differentiation.
Distribute domain partitions across GPUs and accumulate gradients over smaller slices to control peak memory without additional interface loss terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports sharper boundaries, smaller gray areas, and lower volume fractions than a conventional FEM-based approach on 2D benchmarks, plus 3D demonstrations with up to eight million collocation points on eight GPUs.
watch_item: Aggregated stress constraints warrant checking local stress peaks; the abstract does not quantify constraint accuracy or runtime gains.
paper_title: Scalable Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization: A Super-resolution and Simultaneous Approach Based on Machine Learning
